data.title: CORRECTION: Vertical Data Closes $4.24 Million Private Placement of Common Stock
data.description:
This release corrects and updates references to advisory companies and their role in the private placement.

B. Riley Securities acted as placement agent for the offering, which comes as Vertical Data is actively pursuing an uplisting to a national stock exchange in the near future

LAS VEGAS, NV / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Vertical Data Inc. ("Vertical Data" or the "Company") today announced the closing of an approximately $4.24 million private placement of common stock at $3.00 per share for an aggregate of 1,413,640 shares.

Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is acting as exclusive capital markets advisor to Vertical Data. B. Riley Securities acted as placement agent in connection with the private placement.

"We believe a disciplined approach to capital formation is fundamental to building long-term shareholder value," said Chairman and CEO Deven Soni. "By structuring this offering as a straightforward sale of common stock we are maintaining the simplicity and transparency that guides our financing strategy across our platform. We are also actively pursuing an uplisting to a national stock exchange as part of our broader strategy to support Vertical Data's continued growth and expansion."

In connection with the offering, Vertical Data Chairman and CEO Deven Soni bought $500,000 with other insiders purchasing another approximately $500,000 for a total of $1 million, representing approximately 24% of the total proceeds coming from insiders. B. Riley Securities, the placement agent, also participated for $1,000,000. B. Riley Securities participated in a prior offering for $1,175,000 (including principals and employees), which when combined with this offering amounts to a total of $2,175,000.

The shares were offered and sold to accredited investors and to persons outside the United States in reliance on the exemptions from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The Company is required to file a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission covering the resale of the shares within 30 days of the closing.

The securities described above have not been registered under the Securities Act or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from the registration requirements. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any securities, and there shall not be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

About Vertical Data Inc.

Vertical Data Inc. is an AI infrastructure company operating three platforms. VerticalData.io provides enterprise GPU provisioning and managed infrastructure. GPU Financing arranges structured financing for GPU deployments. Vertical Edge holds equity in the data centers the Company sources, develops, leases and manages. Together, the three platforms deliver hardware, financing and facilities under one company. For more information, visit verticaldata.io/investor-relations.

data.title: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from SpaceX board
data.description:
SpaceX disclosed on Friday that Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from the rockets-to-AI company's board after more than a decade.

Here are some details:

  • Harrison notified SpaceX of his resignation on November 4, and it took effect immediately

  • The Elon Musk-led company said Harrison's decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the company on matters relating to its operations, policies or practices

  • Harrison, a longtime executive at Google, is currently president of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development. Google parent Alphabet is the ‌largest single institutional holder of SpaceX, according to LSEG data

  • Musk said that Harrison stepped down because there were too many conflicts of interest with Alphabet. "Don has been a great board member. Very much appreciate his contributions," Musk added in a post on X on Friday.

  • Google on Friday reported a small increase in its position in SpaceX to about 555 million shares from 551.2 million earlier

data.title: America Has Become the Last Place to Make Money for the World's Automakers — WSJ
data.description:
By Sharon Terlep

Volkswagen is considering making its first American pickup in 40 years. Nissan is promising more rugged SUVs. And Detroit is racing to maintain its high margins in the heartland.

The U.S. is emerging as the last true profit engine for the world's carmakers — and the auto industry is scrambling to compete.

"My top three priorities are: U.S.A.," Hyundai CEO José Muñoz said at a recent event, explaining why so many of the South Korean automaker's new models are tailored for American drivers.

U.S., European and Asian automakers are all focused on making and selling cars in the U.S. because of Americans' proclivity for large pickups and SUVs — vehicles with high profit margins — and their willingness to swallow record-high sticker prices. New car prices are hovering around $50,000, while roughly one-fifth of new-vehicle buyers have monthly car payments that top $1,000.

Another reason is that the market in China, for decades the path to automotive dominance, has hit a wall. Sales are down more than 20% through September, creating a massive overcapacity crisis. Other big markets, including Europe, Japan and the Middle East, are also sputtering.

Additionally, the Trump administration eliminated strict emissions and fuel-economy rules that pushed carmakers to make electric vehicles, often at a loss. And the U.S. is insulated — by high tariffs and technology bans — from low-price, high-tech cars being made in China.

Over the last decade, Chinese central and local governments have poured billions into developing the country's homegrown electric-vehicle industry, building with a fraction of Western labor costs.

The low-cost vehicles have conquered overseas markets and battered European automakers on their home turf.

Detroit automakers like General Motors are on the defensive and looking for new revenue streams as overseas rivals target the most profitable and fastest-growing types of vehicles in the U.S.: pickup trucks, SUVs and gas-electric hybrids.

"The United States is the most lucrative auto market in the world," GM finance chief Paul Jacobson said recently. "We've got to be competitive."

Toyota, which has pledged up to $10 billion in U.S. investments, is spending $3.6 billion on a new factory to bring production of its midsize Tacoma pickup back to the U.S. This past week, the company named a new North American chief and said it's weighing whether to add more vehicles at its growing Texas truck factory to help beef up offerings in the region.

Honda is growing its manufacturing presence in Ohio. Hyundai said it aims to launch dozens of new or made-over models in North America by the end of the decade, including off roaders, its first-ever midsize pickup and high-end models from its Genesis brand.

And Nissan is bringing back its beefy Xterra SUV while racing out hybrid versions of its top sellers, including the Rouge SUV, which it launched nearly a year ahead of schedule. CEO Ivan Espinosa said he aims to grow Nissan's U.S. market share to about 7%, up from below 6% today. That would mean more than 160,000 in additional vehicle sales.

European automakers are also rolling out hulking new high-end SUVs for the U.S. market.

Last month, Volkswagen-owned Audi announced a new $4 billion factory in rural Georgia, where it will build big, premium SUVs for American drivers — joining other European companies, including Mercedes and Volvo — that are growing their manufacturing operations and product lines in the U.S.

"The United States is the second-largest premium market in the world, and today we are not fully exploiting this potential," Audi Chief Executive Gernot Döllner said in announcing the move. (Even as sales slump, China is still the world's biggest market for premium vehicles.) "We are changing that," Döllner said.

Though the German automaker is slashing jobs and closing factories elsewhere around the world, Volkswagen executives also said last month the company will look at building and selling trucks in the U.S., even if the Trump administration doesn't pass trade deals with Canada and Mexico to make it more affordable.

It is considering building the trucks in collaboration with another automaker and is in talks with Ford over a potential joint venture, the company said.

That may be easier said than done. A Volkswagen truck would be a direct run at a segment that Detroit has dominated for more than half a century — one that almost no foreign competitors have been able to crack. Only Toyota's Tacoma manages meaningful sales volumes against Ford, GM and Ram trucks.

"It's a market that looks really good from an outsider's perspective," said Sam Fiorani, vice president of global vehicle forecasting at research firm AutoForecast Solutions. "But it's really hard to tap in to." Fiorani estimates new factories planned by automakers will add enough capacity to build more than one million additional vehicles a year in the U.S. by 2030.

The foreign automaker surge promises new choices for American customers and a wave of manufacturing jobs. It also threatens to crowd an already stagnant U.S. auto market — leaving automakers vulnerable to expensive, half-empty factories if demand softens further. Americans are holding on to their cars for longer these days: The average car on U.S. roads is about 13 years old, a historic high.

Jacobson, the GM CFO, said he worries the U.S. market could run into problems with underused factories given how many automakers are adding manufacturing space and capacity. He said GM must keep costs down and resist the urge to grow capacity itself.

As Toyota is closing in on GM's spot as America's top-selling automaker — a title it's held for 100 years — the American manufacturer is racing to build profitable side bets in software subscriptions, battery energy storage and defense contracting.

It's also planning a raft of new products. After long dismissing hybrid technology as an unnecessary detour on the path to EVs, the automaker has made a dramatic about-face as Toyota, Honda and Hyundai see their hybrids drive big sales gains this year.

GM now plans to roll out hybrid versions of many of its most popular vehicles, including a trio of three-row SUVs and the Chevrolet Equinox SUV, its top-selling model behind the Silverado and Sierra pickups, according to people familiar with the matter.

Ford is battling slowing sales with plans for a raft of more affordable models and its much-hyped Fathom electric pickup truck, designed to rival the low-cost and high-tech sheen of Chinese EVs. But while GM has said it won't give priority to growing market share, Ford CEO Jim Farley recently told employees he expects the company to grow global sales by 20% by early next decade.

The company is also looking to Washington, arguing that tariff relief extended by the Trump administration to South Korea and Japan has placed the automaker at a competitive disadvantage to its Asian rivals. Hyundai is creeping up on Ford as No. 3 in the ranking of America's top-selling automakers.

Executives at foreign automakers say they harbor no illusions about the difficulty of growing sales into the U.S.

"It's going to be a challenge as we go forward, but I think we know what the consumer is looking for," said Lance Woelfer, Honda's U.S. sales chief.

Ponz Pandikuthira, Nissan's North American product chief, said: "There's a sense of urgency. U.S. success and profitability is critical." It has been apparent even in his interactions with the Japanese automaker's headquarters.

Now, when he has a question for the boss, he never has to wait for a reply.

"I don't need to wait for a formal meeting to address an issue with the CEO," Pandikuthira said. "I literally send them a WhatsApp message and say, 'I need a quick decision on this, please help.'"

Write to Sharon Terlep at sharon.terlep@wsj.com

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway utility asks California regulators for 57% rate increase
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.B) (BRK.A) Pacific Power utility asked California regulators Friday to approve a 57% rate increase that would hike the typical residential electricity bill by $120/month.

The increase would boost the utility's base revenue by $103M/year and reflects capital spending already under way to safeguard the grid.

Pacific Power's equipment has allegedly been tied to two blazes in California: the 2020 Slater Fire that burned more than 150K and killed two people and the 2022 McKinney Fire that burned 60K acres and killed four people.

Utility President Ryan Flynn told The Wall Street Journal that the company is swapping wooden power poles for steel and fiberglass structures and replacing hundreds of miles of bare wire with insulated, fire-resistant conductor.

Beyond the rate case, Pacific Power faces $637M in liability claims and legal expenses stemming from the 2020 and 2022 fires, and it is asking regulators to let it recover $340.5M of that sum from customers.

Pacific Power's Northern California territory sweeps across 11,292 square miles from the coast to the Nevada border, serving ~46K customers—about four customers per square mile; the utility also operates in Oregon, where it has ~630K customers.

data.title: Bitcoin steadies after record hack fallout, midterm turbulence
data.description:
Bitcoin settled near recent lows after a bruising selloff on Thursday swept through cryptocurrencies and other risky assets, pressured by lackluster chipmaker earnings and a Democratic sweep of Congress.

The largest cryptocurrency was trading mostly little changed at around $75,600 on Friday, having tumbled more than 6% from a position above $80,000 a day earlier. Smaller cryptocurrencies such as BNB, Ether and Solana were broadly flat.

A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market on Friday as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December.

“Bitcoin appears to be finding some relief after yesterday’s sharp selloff, although I would be cautious about calling this a reversal just yet,” Dean Chen, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitunix, said in an email. “I would describe the current move as selling pressure easing, rather than fresh accumulation taking hold.”

Crypto remains on shaky ground after a $6.3 billion hack on digital-asset exchange Binance Holdings Ltd. rocked the sector on Oct. 29, dampening investor enthusiasm for the asset class. Volatility in the broader market has only worsened the blow, with routs in artificial intelligence stocks spilling over to crypto as a result of many of the industry’s mining companies pivoting to the AI industry in recent years.

“The selloff reflects growing doubts over the returns from huge AI spending, fears that tighter regulation could slow data-center construction and a broader retreat from highly valued growth assets,” said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG. “Yet with stock markets continuing to slide, Bitcoin is so far holding its ground, suggesting buyers are stepping in to defend current levels. That relative strength could be an important test of whether Bitcoin is starting to decouple from the technology trade, rather than simply following it lower.”

Spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in the US recorded $430 million in outflows on Thursday, data compiled by Bloomberg show. The Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund led the pack with about $200 million of that figure, followed by BlackRock Inc.’s IBIT with about $105 million in outflows.

“The selling does seem to be easing, but the recent bounce looks more like brief relief than sustained recovery,” said Samuel Leyne, co-head of crypto trading at Marex.

“You need a real catalyst to bring confidence back, whether that’s geopolitics cooling off, oil coming down or the macro picture improving,” he added. “Until then, we have to watch stocks, ETF flows and the basis levels. Bitcoin needs to get back above $77,000 to build any momentum, and if equities keep sliding, $75,000 is right back in play.”

data.title: Corn barge bids ease as shippers focus on soybeans
data.description:
Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast declined on Friday, despite a slowdown in farmer offerings, as Gulf exporters remained busy shipping soybeans, traders said.

  • China continues to book US soybeans. The US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 136,000 metric tons of soybeans to China under its daily reporting rules, along with sales of 101,000 tons of corn to undisclosed destinations.

  • China has committed to purchasing at least 25 million metric tons of US soybeans for the 2026-27 marketing year that began on September 1. By October 22, China had purchased 15.1 million tons of US soy and shipped 5.9 million tons, according to a report issued this week by the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service.

  • The Midwest harvest is winding down, but rains earlier this week slowed the last stages of fieldwork. Drier weather was expected through next week.

  • Growers in western Illinois and eastern Missouri were about three weeks from completing the harvest, one merchandiser said.

  • Farmer grain sales stalled this week as Chicago Board of Trade corn (CZ26) and soybean (SF27) futures hit multimonth lows. "The farmer is super disengaged," one broker said.

  • At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 86 cents over Chicago Board of Trade December (CZ26) futures, down 3 cents from Thursday.

  • FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in December held steady at around 110 cents over futures.

  • For soybeans, CIF barges loaded in November were bid at 105 cents over CBOT January soybean (SF27) futures, down 1 cent from Thursday.

  • FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in December were steady at about 118 cents over January futures.

  • Ahead of the USDA's monthly supply/demand report on November 10, analysts on average expected the agency to lower its US corn yield estimate and raise its soybean yield estimate.
